title: Linear backlog export row
description: Schema for one row of analysis/handoff/backlog_export_linear.csv produced by bsa-backlog-bridge (Phase 3, US-S9-02). Linear's CSV import accepts a column subset (Title, Description, Status, Priority, Labels, Assignee, Estimate); the bridge emits exactly that subset plus BSA provenance columns (StoryID, SourceClaimIDs, RelatedNFRIDs) so the export is idempotent + traceable. Read-only with respect to canonical state. Schema-enforced via F5 dispatcher entry under analysis/handoff/backlog_export_linear.csv.

Title.description: Linear issue title. Sourced from A70.Title.

Description.description: Markdown body: A70.StoryText followed by an 'Acceptance criteria' section. Linear renders Markdown natively.

Status.description: Initial Linear status. Bridge defaults to 'Backlog' for INVEST-deferred stories (INVESTStatus != 'pass') and 'Todo' for INVEST-pass stories. Closed statuses (In Progress, Done, Canceled) are out of scope — Linear teams own lifecycle post-import.

Priority.description: Linear priority (1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium). Maps from A70.Priority: level-1 → 1, level-2 → 2, level-3 → 3.

Labels.description: Comma-separated Linear labels. Schema enforces (via 3 positive + 3 negative lookaheads) that the comma list contains EXACTLY ONE of each required tag class: 'bsa-export' provenance tag + a 'level-1|2|3' priority tier (mapping verbatim from A70.Priority) + an 'invest-*' tier (one of pass / needs-splitting / needs-estimation / needs-testable-acceptance / needs-negotiation / escalate, prefixed). Negative lookaheads catch contradictory duplicates: 'bsa-export,level-1,level-2,invest-pass' (two priority tiers), 'bsa-export,level-1,invest-pass,invest-needs-estimation' (two INVEST tiers — Linear has no separate INVESTStatus field to disambiguate, so this would be silently broken), and duplicate 'bsa-export' all fail validation. Per-tag character class is lowercase + alphanumeric + hyphen + underscore. Operators may add extra labels post-export; the schema accepts any number of extras as long as the three required-tag classes appear EXACTLY ONCE each.

Estimate.description: Linear estimate (Fibonacci). Maps from A70.EstimationHint: xs→1, s→2, m→3, l→5, xl→8, unknown→empty string. Empty string is the explicit 'no hint' value (Linear leaves the field blank on import).

StoryID.description: Provenance: A70.StoryID. Linear stores this as a custom field (or in description footer if customfields are unavailable on the team's plan). Required for downstream drift detection.

SourceClaimIDs.description: Provenance: A70.SourceClaimIDs verbatim (semicolon/slash list). Empty allowed when RelatedNFRIDs is non-empty (mirrors A70 INV-08).

RelatedNFRIDs.description: Provenance: A70.RelatedNFRIDs verbatim. Empty allowed when SourceClaimIDs is non-empty.

x-bsa-csv-columns-order._comment: Canonical column order for diff stability. Linear-import-required columns first (Title..Estimate), BSA provenance columns after. Re-running the bridge produces byte-identical output (apart from the source A70 timestamp embedded in any free-text bodies the operator added).

x-bsa-provenance-rules._comment: INV-08 carries through to the export — every row MUST carry non-empty SourceClaimIDs OR RelatedNFRIDs (mirrors A70 schema's same-named extension). Reuses the generalized _apply_provenance_rules handler in write_validator.py — same hook-time enforcement as A70 itself.
x-bsa-provenance-rules.rationale: An export row with both provenance fields empty would be a backlog item the consumer can't trace back to a claim or NFR — defeats the whole point of the bridge. Schema-enforced at write time so a bridge bug emitting empty provenance fails the F5 hook.
